title: PixelForge — an original pixel-grid type family
headline: Forged on the pixel grid.
lede: Nine weights and nine pixel-step italics drawn on a 5×8 master grid. From hairline Thin to heavy Black, every stem stays on the grid and every counter stays open.
presets: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.
sections: Each glyph is a hand-drawn pixel map in sources/pixelmaps.txt. The engine turns pixels into rectangles, bridges orthogonal neighbours, and joins diagonal neighbours with an explicit pixel step at light weights. At heavy weights, ink can only grow a fixed amount into a one-pixel counter, so m, e, B and 8 stay open. Italics shift each row by 16 units: a stepped slant, never a shear, so pixel rows stay horizontal.
Square O, notched 0, a tailed l against a serifed I, and a hooked 1. The zero feature gives a slashed zero and ss01 a dotted one.
Box drawing, block elements, shades as a pixel dither, and Powerline separators drawn with 50-unit stair steps.
install_html:
mkdir -p ~/.local/share/fonts/PixelForge
unzip PixelForge-v1.000.zip -d ~/.local/share/fonts/PixelForge
fc-cache -f ~/.local/share/fonts
fc-list | grep PixelForge

Web: <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/pixelforge.css"> then font-family: "PixelForge";. Nix: nix build github:r3dg0d/pixelforge-font.
footer: PixelForge · OFL-1.1 · built from source with fontTools, ufo2ft and pathops
